facts.text: Happy Valley was originally called Wong Nai Chung Valley, meaning "yellow mud stream," and was the only flat land on north side of Hong Kong Island.
In 1846 the British cleared rice paddies to build the Happy Valley Racecourse, the first horse racing track in Hong Kong.
The area became a burial ground during early colonial days when malaria killed many soldiers, leading to the name Happy Valley as a euphemism for cemeteries.
Happy Valley hosts the Hong Kong Racing Museum and the Hong Kong Jockey Club clubhouse, preserving the region’s racing heritage.
The Wong Nai Chung Public Library sits in the municipal services building, offering residents a quiet spot amid the valley’s green spaces.
A historic cemetery dating back to the 1800s, Happy Valley Cemetery, lies within the valley and reflects its early colonial past.
